rendered: The document does not say the authors ran a long melt-diffusion step. The long melt route appears only as a description of other groups' methods: the paper says other methods traditionally employ long (>20 h) melt[1] techniques to ensure pore infiltration. The authors' own sulfur infiltration is an isothermal vapor phase process[2]. The stated reason for preferring it is that it is significantly more scalable and less expensive compared to[3] those long melt methods. The authors' infiltration temperature was 175 °C[4], and it lasted 1 h[5]. The paper gives no further rationale for the choice of temperature or duration.
